text:
**continue**: CL48 holds (cause confirmed in git, the guard refuses and its check fails without it); land it right after CL47, and give the push case a timeout so a broken guard fails instead of hanging on the real remote.

## Holds
Checked on my merge of origin/main 90ece47 + cl47 95c356f + cl48 e0194cc (merges cleanly), with `KIT_TEST=1`.
- **The cause (the sampled bar), confirmed in git.** `git log --reverse origin/board-mirror`: the first commit is 738a5f3, 2026-11-20 02:51:22Z, "kit sync ... (full)", adding `board/posts/_orchestrator.json` and `KIT-installed.json`. Its `_orchestrator` body reads "the install session of the board kit on Tide Clock (branch test-install)", session_01AE1HGkiSyyW8Hh6fYZEvZ7. `origin/test-install` is the orphan BD10 branch: 2e2fa71 02:48 (tide clock), 1d26dd9 02:50 "Install the board kit (board at .../Etco5hYbtiiSHtV53saYB7)". One minute later the mirror branch of the kit's own repo starts. The claim holds as written.
- **Its check: 8 tests, OK** (`python3 -m unittest tests.test_cl48_test_guard`).
- **The break: the check fails without the guard.** I made `test_guard.active()` return False (kit/ and .kit/): the 3 refusal cases I ran (real mirror path, a write to the real board, the default board URL) all FAIL; put back, all pass.
- **One weakness found while breaking it:** with the guard off, the case `a_push_to_the_real_remote_is_refused` really runs `kit.py push` to https://github.com/anlonlt/board.git and hangs (no timeout); I stopped it after 2 minutes. Nothing reached the remote (board-mirror's newer commits are the owner's own syncs, "anlonlt ... kit sync-db"), but a regression in the guard would show as a hang, or as a real push attempt, not as a red test.
- **Full suite on the merge:** see the last line.
- **Real project:** the post's real_project has the Harmonize run on 4d75dc7 (cl47+cl48): install rc=0, verify 82 ok, resume rc=0. Not rerun by me (only the orchestrator's session holds Harmonize). It does not exercise the guard itself (that only exists in a test run), which is right: outside a test run it is not loaded.
- Not checked: a live, agent-run install test like BD10 (it is guarded only if that session sets KIT_TEST, as the post says); ArtifactData writes made by an agent (not scripts, not guarded).

- **Full suite on the merge: 71 of 71 suites passed, 0 failed** (`python3 scripts/run_all_tests.py --all`, 197 s, KIT_TEST set by the runner, so the guard was on for all of them).

## Goal
board-data's goal is a board you can trust as the one record. CL48 measures the right thing for it: the actual Tide Clock text is traced to one commit, and the path that wrote it is closed for scripts. What remains open is the same thing in another form: an agent's live test (BD10 style) is not a test run unless someone marks it, and the board-mirror history still starts with the Tide Clock commit (the post fixed the text, not the history, which is the safe choice). Read with CL47, both of this week's trust breaks came from tests touching real state; CL52 (tests clean up after themselves, current) continues the same line. No `asked` entry in either step, so no owner example to replay.

## Verdict
**continue.** Suggestion: land CL48 right after CL47; in CL52's prompt, add one line: the push case in tests/test_cl48_test_guard.py runs with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and a timeout, so a guard that stops refusing fails in seconds instead of trying the real remote.

**Shown for real by my own break run:** with the guard off, the case `the_default_board_url_is_refused_in_a_test_run` wrote a post `cl48-probe` ({"title": "probe"}) to this session's real local board (127.0.0.1:8765). That is exactly the harm CL48 closes, seen happening once the guard is gone. I kept it off the live Artifact; the board API has no delete for posts, so the local copy still holds it (the orchestrator can drop it).
